newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bibby shares on the way to 150p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bibby shares on the way to 150p.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-50 * MA-200
+ Recent chart breakout at 130p by shares in Bibby (J) & Sons implies further gains up to 150p, technical analysts said.
+ There is added significance to the breakout owing to the inordinate length of time the shares have spent moving sideways between 108p and 130p.
+ Bibby's medium and long-term moving averages are sloping upwards indicating further share price strength, analysts added.
Shares in diversified industrials company Bibby (J) & Sons have broken above 130p chart resistance leaving them a clear run up to 150p, technical analysts said.

"The shares of this smaller diversified industrials company have broken higher after being in a consolidation band since July last year," said Richard Marshall, a director at Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd.
"An initial target at 150p can be expected from the breakout although longer-term there seems no reason why the 1992 peak around 180p will not be challenged," he added.
By 1030 GMT Bibby shares had added 2-1/2p to 133-1/2p.
Since July 1995 they had been trapped between 108p and 130p but from the low point of 108p in July they have trended higher.

"In the past month the shares have been in a narrower trading band between 126p and 130p," said Marshall, adding there was chart support from the stock's rising 50-day moving average which is currently at 126p.
The shares climbed above their 50-day moving average line in late July and have made ground against that line indicating share price strength.
But relative to the All-Share index, Bibby's shares have merely kept up with the stock market over the long-term although over short periods they have been volatile.
"The relative strength line has shown little deterioration during the past 12 months consolidation and the (stock's) 200 day moving average is now also supporting the share price," said Marshall.
And the combination of gentle upward-sloping moving averages and a neutral relative strength line implies a gradual share price strength, he added.
